## Introduction 
First discovered in 1996 in seminal work by [@Bentin1996],
the N170 component is an event related potential that has a negative polarity (hence the “N” in N170). The component occurs at a latency of 170ms post stimulus, and its topography tends to be around the occipital-temporal area and is typically right-lateralized, meaning the negative deflection is usually larger on the right hemisphere [@Bentin1996]. 
The functional aspect of the component is believed to reflect the brains’ ability or tendency to distinguish between a facial stimulus and an object. The component is elicited under conditions where facial stimuli are presented or manipulated. component has been observed as present even if a facial stimulus only contains the eyes/ and eye area [@Itier2007].

Understanding this component may help researchers and physicians understand a multitude of psychiatric conditions, such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), social anxiety, prospagnosia (face blindness), dementia and schizophrenia. 

### Controversy Surrounding the Component

The N170 ERP component has been the subject of considerable debate regarding its functional significance and neural origins. While some researchers argue that it reflects neural processes specific to face perception [@Bentin1996] [@Eimer2011] others suggest that it may reflect broader visual recognition mechanisms shaped by experience and expertise, which also extend to familiar non-face objects [@Gauthier2000] . Furthermore, questions remain about the extent to which the N170 is genuinely face-specific, with evidence suggesting that its response may be influenced by the perceptual characteristics of visual stimuli [@Thierry2007]. Overall, although the N170 is widely recognised as an important marker of early face processing, its precise functional role and neural generators remain debated.



## Methods

Data was gathered from the ERP CORE @kappenman2021 resource under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0). 

### Participants

Note: Three particpants were excluded, refer to the code below for particpants ID's 

```{python}
# participants excluded
EXCLUDE = ["001", "005", "016"]
```

The ERP CORE resource contains data from 40 participants (25 female, 15 male; age M = 21.5 years, SD = 2.87, range 18-30; 38 right-handed; @kappenman2021). Following the exclusion criteria applied by @kappenman2021, three participants were excluded. Participants 1 and 16 had fewer than 50% of face trials remaining after artifact rejection, and participant 5 had artifacts on more than 25% of trials (as listed in the resource's Subject_Summary spreadsheet). The final sample consisted of 37 participants (24 female, 13 male; age M = 21.5 years, SD = 2.96, range 18-30; 35 right-handed). 

### Procedure

The N170 was elicited by a face perception task that @kappenman2021 adapted from [@Rossion2011]. On each trial, a single image of a face, a car, a scrambled face or a scrambled car appeared at the centre of the screen for 300 ms, followed by a blank interval of 1100-1300 ms. Participants judged whether each image was an "object" (face or car) or a "texture" (scrambled face or scrambled car). The N170 is isolated by contrasting faces with cars.

### EEG recording

EEG was recorded with a Biosemi ActiveTwo system using active electrodes mounted in an elastic cap. Thirty scalp sites followed the International 10/20 system. The common mode sense (CMS) electrode was at PO1 and the driven right leg (DRL) electrode at PO2. Horizontal EOG was recorded from electrodes lateral to the external canthus of each eye, and vertical EOG from an electrode below the right eye. Signals were low-pass filtered during recording (cutoff 204.8 Hz) and digitised at 1024 Hz. Referencing was performed offline [@kappenman2021].

### Analysis parameters

Parameters followed the values recommended for the N170 by @kappenman2021, except for the filter and artifact-rejection settings, which followed the course pipeline.  


#### Preprocessing parameters

Data were re-referenced to the average of all electrodes, following @kappenman2021, who used an average reference for the N170. The signal was band-pass filtered between 0.1 and 30 Hz. [@kappenman2021] applied a 0.1 Hz high-pass filter and corrected ocular artifacts with independent component analysis (ICA), which was not part of the present pipeline. 

```{python}

FILTER_SETTINGS = {
    "low_cutoff": 0.1,
    "high_cutoff": 30.0
}

# This setting re-references to the average of all scalp electrodes
REFERENCE = None

```

#### Epoching parameters

The selected electrode was PO8 and the analysis window was 136ms to 176ms, shifted 26ms after the course notes 110 - 150ms recomendation. The epoch window was -200ms to 800ms, and thus the baseline was -200ms.

```{python}
TMIN = -0.2 
TMAX = 0.8  

BASELINE = (-0.2,0) # baseline interval

# critical conditions for averaging and epoching
CONDITIONS = ["stimulus/face", "stimulus/car"]

REJECT = {
    "eeg": 150e-6,
    "eog": 250e-6
}

```

## Data analysis

### Preprocessing

Each raw file was re-referenced and filtered with the custom preprocessing function (scripts/preprocpy), using the reference and filter settings, and the processed data was saved to the data/processed file.

```{python}
#| eval: true # set this to false if you don't want preprocessing to recompute
#| output: false # this suppresses any output

for raw_file in RAW_PATH.glob("*_raw.fif.gz"):

    # extract subject number
    subj_ID = raw_file.stem.split("_")[0]

    # read in raw file 
    raw = SimpleRaw(raw_file)

    # preprocess raw file
    # note how we draw on a custom preprocessing function here
    processed = preprocess(raw, 
                            reref_params = REFERENCE, 
                            filter_low_cutoff = FILTER_SETTINGS["low_cutoff"], 
                            filter_high_cutoff = FILTER_SETTINGS["high_cutoff"])
    
    processed.save(PROCESSED_PATH / f"{subj_ID}_raw.fif.gz", overwrite = True)


```

### Epoching and averaging

For each included participant, the processed data were epoched (-200 to 800 ms, baseline -200 to 0 ms with the rejection thresholds above) and the epochs for faces and cars were averaged separately.
```{python}
#| output: false

# initialise empty dictionary to hold single-subject averages
ss_avs = {}

for cond in CONDITIONS:
    ss_avs[cond] = []

for processed_file in PROCESSED_PATH.glob("*_raw.fif.gz"):

    # extract subject number
    subj_ID = processed_file.stem.split("_")[0]

    # check to see if participant should be excluded
    if subj_ID in EXCLUDE:
        # skip the rest of the loop and move on to the next participant
        continue

    # read in preprocessed file
    processed = SimpleRaw(processed_file)

    # extract events
    events, event_id = processed.get_events()

    # epoch data
    epochs = SimpleEpoch(processed, events, event_id, tmin = TMIN, tmax = TMAX, baseline = BASELINE, reject = REJECT)

    # subset epochs and average by condition 
    for cond in CONDITIONS:
        av = epochs[cond].average()
        ss_avs[cond].append(av)

```

### Grand average

The single-participant averages for each condition were averaged across the 37 participants to create the grand averages.

```{python}
#| output: false

# create an empty dict to hold our grand averages
grand_avs = {}

for cond in CONDITIONS:
    grand = grand_average(ss_avs[cond])
    grand_avs[cond] = grand
```

## Results 

The plot shows the grand average ERPs for faces and cars at PO8 (N = 37), with negative voltage plotted upward. The dashed vertical lines mark the analysis window of 136-176 ms, which is the window recommended by @kappenman2021 (110-150 ms) shifted 26 ms later. Both conditions show an early positive peak of about 5-6 µV at around 125-140 ms. Within the analysis window, the face waveform becomes negative, reaching about -1.8 µV at approximately 170 ms, whereas the car waveform stays close to zero and does not become negative. The face deflection occurs roughly 15-20 ms earlier than the car waveform's peak.
```{python} 
selected_electrode = "PO8"
plot_title = "Grand average for N170: Faces versus cars"
analysis_window_start = 0.136   
analysis_window_end = 0.176     
```

### Grand average: 
Depicted below is the grand average plot of the representative electrode (PO8) 
```{python}
selected_electrode = "PO8"
plot_title = "Grand average for N170: Faces versus cars"
analysis_window_start = 0.136   # or 0.136 for the 26 ms shift
analysis_window_end = 0.176     # or 0.176 for the 26 ms shift

plot_evokeds(grand_avs, picks = selected_electrode, invert_y = True, title = plot_title, vlines = [analysis_window_start, analysis_window_end])


```

## Discussion and reflection


The replication in the present paper mimics the results of @kappenman2021 well. There is a clear difference between the car condition and the face condition within the analysis window across both the N170 grand averages. While this report replicated well and produced similar results to @kappenman2021, the abscence of the independant component analysis (ICA) stage could have been the cause of any discrepancies between the two plots.
